fieldValues.title: Who may extend an affirmation to the parts of a whole
fieldValues.decision_question: When the owner has affirmed a whole (a tension) but never saw some of its parts (its poles), may an agent put those parts into Affirmed, or must the owner affirm them with them in view?
fieldValues.friction:
The repair in srs-programme#536 cannot finish without either an agent writing into Affirmed or the owner acting on 17 tensions again.
- If it is left, readers keep mixing layers. The tension card planned in srs-web#581 would show an affirmed trade-off whose two sides are still suggestions.
- The owner keeps being asked about things they believe they settled ("I ratified them all yesterday?", vignette 32683192).
- Every extra act adds to the load the owner has named: "too difficult and so we never get there".
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. Do nothing: leave the 34 suggested poles inside the 17 affirmed tensions.
- Leads to: the layers stay mixed, and each reader resolves it its own way. The srs-web#581 card shows affirmed trade-offs with suggested sides. Tensions already affirmed cannot use the one-act affirm. Pole: neither; the gap stays.

B. Owner only, one act per whole: an agent never creates an Affirmed record. Each of the 17 tensions is put back to the owner once, in the srs-web#581 card with both poles in view, and one tick forks its missing poles.
- Leads to: Affirmed keeps meaning "the owner judged this, with it in view". It costs 17 owner acts, and the repair of these poles waits for srs-web#581. Pole: Semantic integrity.

C. Affirming a whole affirms its nested parts: an agent forks the 34 poles into Affirmed now. Each fork is stamped AI-created, cites the owner's affirmation of the tension, carries an explaining comment, and can be undone by set aside.
- Leads to: no owner acts, and the repair completes now. Affirmed then means "the owner judged this, or the whole it belongs to". Pole descriptions the owner may never have read gain the owner's authority. Pole: Practical expression.

D. A provisional state: an agent forks the poles into Affirmed but holds them for review until the owner confirms.
- Leads to: a third state inside the affirmation layer, so two ways to mean affirmed (against one way per goal). The owner still has to act on each. Pole: Practical expression, partly.
fieldValues.key_requirements:
- Affirmed must mean one thing that a reader can rely on without asking who wrote it. It is the anchor the owner says affirmations are (vignette 8b5b80d6).
- The owner's load must fall, not rise: SP-102, and finding deedb2d5 (up to 14 acts per domain).
- One way per goal: no second meaning of affirmed and no third layer state.
- The cost of B is real. Under the owner's own principle that affirmation should be rare, the 17 acts argue for C. The counter-argument is that the poles are not mechanical parts: their looks_like and shadow are claims of their own.
- Placed on Versioning and Reference: B follows the affirmed lean b3ac3391, and C and D go against it. Going against the lean is never a choice, so it is put to the owner.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Every record in Affirmed is created by the owner's own act with that record in view, and an affirmation of a whole carries to its parts only when the parts are shown with it at the moment of affirming.
fieldValues.rationale: Option B follows the affirmed lean Semantic integrity over practical expression. Its boundary keeps meaning at the meaning layer and lets convenience be added on top, and srs-web#581's one-act affirm is that added layer: it lowers the cost without moving the meaning. Under C, Affirmed would stop being evidence that the owner judged a record. That is the same pass-through failure the owner has already named (findings c5a6f672 and da9d4da6): an affirmation that has not seen its content. B's cost is bounded at 17 single acts, each made with the whole in view.
fieldValues.revisit_when:
Revisit toward C (parts carry with their whole) if:
- the owner, shown the 17 tensions with their poles, affirms almost all the poles unchanged, about nine in ten as pass-through. That would mean the parts carry no separate judgement;
- or the per-whole acts become the owner's main affirmation load after srs-web#581 ships.

Revisit if any agent-created record is found in Affirmed. The indicator is records in Affirmed whose createdBy is an AI actor, which should be 0.
fieldValues.next_steps: srs-programme#536 (steps 1, 3 and 5 go ahead; step 2 waits on this decision); srs-web#581 (the card and the one-act affirm that option B relies on).
